messages.subject: Interaction plot & bar plot
messages.body_plain: Hi, does anyone know how to draw a bar plot which looks like an interaction plot and have two categorical independent variables and one interval dependent variable? Thanks!
messages.body_snippet: Hi, does anyone know how to draw a bar plot which looks like an interaction plot and have two categorical independent variables and one interval dependent variable? Thanks!

messages.subject: Re: [StatForLing with R] Interaction plot & bar plot
messages.subject_clean: [StatForLing with R] Interaction plot & bar plot
messages.body_plain:
> Hi, does anyone know how to draw a bar plot which looks like an interaction plot and have two categorical independent variables and one interval dependent variable? Thanks!

Like this?

rm(list=ls(all=TRUE)); set.seed(1)
dv <- rnorm(200)
iv1 <- factor(sample(letters[1:2], 200, replace=TRUE))
iv2 <- factor(sample(letters[11:12], 200, replace=TRUE))
(qwe <- tapply(dv, list(iv1, iv2), mean))
barplot(qwe, beside=TRUE)

Best,
STG
--
Stefan Th. Gries

Univ. of California, Santa Barbara
http://tinyurl.com/stgries

messages.subject_clean: How to change the order of groups in a factor variable without changing other corresponding variable
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
    I tried the following script to change the order of groups in a factor, but I found as a result, the groups with the changed order can't match with other variables which used to correspond these groups. So what's the solution? (imagine I have three groups for a variable). Thanks!

variableName<-factor(variableName, levles = levels(variableName)[c(2,1, 3)])

Best,
Grace

messages.body_plain:
set.seed is for setting a seed ;) for the pseudo-random generator in your computer. That way you always get the same "random" numbers. rnorm produces random numbers based on the normal distribution, tapply applies a function to a data set but by groups according to a given factor. I'd suggest using "?rnorm", "?set.seed", and "?tapply".
